title: Inverse for a residue-compatible ind-etale quotient map over two bases
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ be a commutative local ring, let $J\subseteq\mathfrak m_R$ be an ideal, and put $S=R/J$. Let $C$ be a strictly henselian local ring and $D$ a henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], equipped with local structure maps $R\to C$ and $S\to D$. Assume that $C$ is a filtered colimit of etale $R$-algebras and $D$ is a filtered colimit of etale $S$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Let $K$ be a field and fix residue-field identifications $C/\mathfrak m_C\cong K$ and $D/\mathfrak m_D\cong K$ such that $R\to C\to K$ and $R\to S\to D\to K$ agree and have kernel $\mathfrak m_R$. Suppose $u:C\to D$ is a local $R$-algebra map, where the $R$-action on $D$ is through $S$, and that its residue map is $\mathrm{id}_K$. Put $Q=C/JC$, let $q:C\to Q$ be the quotient map, and equip $Q$ with the $S$-action induced from $R\to C\to Q$. Then $Q$ is henselian local with maximal ideal $q(\mathfrak m_C)$, and the residue map induced by $q$ identifies its residue field with $K$. The unique factored $S$-algebra map $\bar u:Q\to D$ satisfying $\bar u\circ q=u$ is an isomorphism. More precisely there is a unique local $S$-algebra map $v:D\to Q$ inducing $\mathrm{id}_K$, and it satisfies $\bar u\circ v=\mathrm{id}_D$ and $v\circ u=q$, hence $v\circ\bar u=\mathrm{id}_Q$. Consequently $u$ is surjective and $\ker(u)=JC$.

source.place: Tag 08HR (lemma-map-into-henselian-colimit), applied over S twice and R once, following the inverse-composite argument of Tag 08HT (lemma-uniqueness-henselian).

proof.text: Since $R\to C$ is local and $J\subseteq\mathfrak m_R$, the image of $J$ lies in $\mathfrak m_C$, and hence $JC\subseteq\mathfrak m_C$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-quotient] to $C$ and $JC$. It gives that $Q=C/JC$ is strictly henselian local, with maximal ideal $q(\mathfrak m_C)$ and residue field canonically $C/\mathfrak m_C=K$. In particular $Q$ is henselian. The equality $q^{-1}(q(\mathfrak m_C))=\mathfrak m_C$ follows from $\ker q=JC\subseteq\mathfrak m_C$, so $q$ is local.

source.place: Tag 05WS (lemma-quotient-strict-henselization), quotient consequence stated in lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-quotient; Tag 04GF (definition-henselian).

proof.text: The $R$-action on $D$ kills $J$, so $u$ kills every generator of $JC$ and thus kills $JC$. The quotient universal property gives a unique ring map $\bar u:Q\to D$ with $\bar u q=u$. For $s\in S$, choose a lift $r\in R$; $R$-linearity of $u$ gives $\bar u(s\cdot1_Q)=s\cdot1_D$, independently of the lift because $J$ acts by zero. Thus $\bar u$ is an $S$-algebra map. Writing $\rho_C,\rho_Q,\rho_D$ for reduction to the specified $K$, one has $\rho_Qq=\rho_C$ and $\rho_D\bar u q=\rho_Du=\rho_C$; surjectivity of $q$ gives $\rho_D\bar u=\rho_Q$. Taking kernels shows that $\bar u$ is local and its residue map is $\mathrm{id}_K$.

Put $\mathfrak m_S=\mathfrak m_R/J$. The residue maps $S\to D\to K$ and $S\to Q\to K$ agree: their composites with the surjection $R\to S$ agree by hypothesis and $\rho_Qq=\rho_C$. Their kernels are $\mathfrak m_S$. Therefore $\mathfrak m_D$ lies over $\mathfrak m_S$ and $\mathrm{id}_K:\kappa(\mathfrak m_D)\to Q/\mathfrak m_Q$, using the specified identifications, is compatible over $\kappa(\mathfrak m_S)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-map-into-henselian-colimit] with base $S$, source the given ind-etale $S$-algebra $D$, target the henselian ring $Q$, and source prime $\mathfrak m_D$. It gives exactly one local $S$-algebra map $v:D\to Q$ with residue map $\mathrm{id}_K$.

Both $\bar u v$ and $\mathrm{id}_D$ are $S$-algebra maps $D\to D$, are local, and induce $\mathrm{id}_K$. Apply uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-map-into-henselian-colimit] with base $S$, source $D$, target the given henselian ring $D$, source prime $\mathfrak m_D$ over $\mathfrak m_S$, and prescribed residue map $\mathrm{id}_K$. Compatibility over $\kappa(\mathfrak m_S)$ holds because both residue-field structures come from the same map $S\to D$. Thus $\bar u v=\mathrm{id}_D$.

Both $vu$ and $q$ are local $R$-algebra maps $C\to Q$ inducing $\mathrm{id}_K$. Apply uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-map-into-henselian-colimit] with base $R$, source the given ind-etale $R$-algebra $C$, target $Q$, source prime $\mathfrak m_C$, and prescribed residue map $\mathrm{id}_K$. The inverse image of $\mathfrak m_Q$ in $R$ and that of $\mathfrak m_C$ in $R$ are $\mathfrak m_R$; the two maps $\kappa(\mathfrak m_R)\to K$ agree by the original residue compatibility. All hypotheses therefore hold, giving $vu=q$. This application is over $R$, not over $S$; no $S$-algebra structure on $C$ is required.

For $x\in Q$, choose $c\in C$ with $q(c)=x$. Then $v\bar u(x)=vu(c)=q(c)=x$. Together with $\bar u v=\mathrm{id}_D$ this proves that $\bar u$ is an isomorphism with inverse $v$. For $d\in D$, choose $c$ with $q(c)=v(d)$; then $u(c)=\bar u v(d)=d$, proving surjectivity of $u$. Finally $u(c)=0$ if and only if $q(c)=0$ since $u=\bar u q$ and $\bar u$ is injective, so $\ker(u)=JC$.
